SAMLLMClientMetadata.description: Smarter API LLMClient Manifest - Metadata class.

annotations.description:
The manifest annotations. Used for storing arbitrary metadata as
            key-value pairs. Example: [{'smarter.sh/test-manifest/project-name': 'Scooby dooby do'}]. The
            key should be a valid url-friendly string. The value accepts
            multi-line string values (YAML block scalars) and various scalar types including
            str, int, float, bool, datetime.date, datetime.datetime, decimal.Decimal, uuid.UUID, bytes, list, dict.

SAMLLMClientMetadata.title: SAMLLMClientMetadata

apiKey.description: LLMClient.spec.apiKey[str]. Optional. The name of the API key that this llmclient uses for authentication. Example: 'my_api_key'. API keys are only necessary for llmclients that are not public facing. This is the name of the API key that is used to authenticate the llmclient with the Smarter API. API keys are issued by a Smarter platform administrator and are used to authenticate the llmclient with the Smarter API.
apiKey.title: Apikey

config.description: LLMClient.spec.config[object]. The configuration for the LLMClient.

functions.description: LLMClient.spec.functions[list]. Optional. The built-in Smarter Functions to add to the LLMClient. Example: ['get_current_weather']. These are built-in backing functions written in Python that are fully compatible with OpenAI API-compatible function calling. These are not the same as OpenAI functions. See https://docs.smarter.sh/ for more information.
functions.title: Functions

guardrails.description: LLMClient.spec.guardrails[list]. Optional. The names of the Guardrails that protect the LLMClient's prompts. Example: ['pii_redaction_input', 'prompt_injection_keyword_input']. Each must be a Guardrail that you own, or that is shared with you, such as Smarter's built-in guardrails. Input guardrails run on the user's message before it is sent to the LLM, and output guardrails on the LLM's reply before it is returned to the user, in order of their priority. Experimental.
guardrails.title: Guardrails

mcpClients.description: LLMClient.spec.mcpClients[list]. Optional. The names of the MCPClients whose MCP servers' tools the LLMClient offers the LLM. Example: ['deepwiki']. Each must be an MCPClient that you own, or that is shared with you. Experimental.
mcpClients.title: Mcpclients

plugins.description: LLMClient.spec.searchTerms[list]. Optional. The Plugins to add to the LLMClient. Plugins are a proprietary extensibility model for tool calling and are not the same as OpenAI plugins. See https://docs.smarter.sh/plugins/ for more information.
plugins.title: Plugins

SAMLLMClientSpecConfig.description:
Smarter API LLMClient Manifest LLMClient.spec.config.

``prompt``, which is required, configures the LLMClient, and ``styles``, which is optional, the
look of its chat.

Manifests written before the split have their settings directly in ``spec.config``. Apply
rejects them, with an error that says where each setting belongs now. See
:meth:`smarter.apps.llmclient.manifest.brokers.llmclient.SAMLLMClientBroker.raise_for_unknown_keys`.

prompt.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt[object]. Required. The LLMClient's LLM provider, model and system prompt, the text of its chat, and where it is published.

styles.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.styles[object]. Optional. The look of the LLMClient's chat, in the Smarter workbench and on every page that embeds it: its logo, background image, fonts and colors. See https://docs.smarter.sh/en/latest/smarter-resources/llmclient/styles.html

SAMLLMClientSpecConfig.title: SAMLLMClientSpecConfig

SAMLLMClientSpecConfigPrompt.description:
Smarter API LLMClient Manifest LLMClient.spec.config.prompt.

What the LLMClient is and does: its LLM provider, model and system prompt, the text of its chat
(its name, welcome message, example prompts and placeholder), and where it is published.

allowedOrigins.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.allowed_origins[list[str]]. Optional. The origins of the web pages that may call this llmclient from a browser, with the @smarter.sh/ui-chat React component, in addition to those that the Smarter platform allows. An origin is a scheme, a host and an optional port, without a path or a wildcard. Example: ['https://www.example.com', 'http://localhost:5173'].
allowedOrigins.title: Allowedorigins

appAssistant.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_assistant[str]. Optional. The assistant name of the llmclient. Example: 'Joe'. This is the fictitious assistant name that will be displayed to users in the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appAssistant.title: Appassistant

appExamplePrompts.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_example_prompts[list]. Optional. A list of example prompts to add to new prompt sessions. These are intended to be brief, and the list is assumed to include only a few examples. Example: ['How do I get a refund?', 'What is the return policy?']. These are intended to help the user to understand the llmclient's capabilities. These will be displayed to users in the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appExamplePrompts.title: Appexampleprompts

appFileAttachment.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_file_attachment[bool]. Optional. Whether the llmclient supports file attachments. Defaults to False. When set to True, a file attachment button will be displayed in the prompt input box of the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appFileAttachment.title: Appfileattachment

appInfoUrl.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_info_url[str]. Optional. The custom info URL of the llmclient. This is a user control button located on the right-hand side of the header of the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appInfoUrl.title: Appinfourl

appName.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_name[str]. Optional. The name of the llmclient. Example: 'Sales Support LLMClient'. This is the name that will be displayed to users in the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appName.title: Appname

appPlaceholder.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_placeholder[str]. Optional. The text placeholder added to the prompt input box for all new prompt sessions. Example: 'ask me anything...'. The place holder will be displayed to users in the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appPlaceholder.title: Appplaceholder

appWelcomeMessage.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.app_welcome_message[str]. Optional. The welcome message of the llmclient. Example: 'Welcome to Smarter's sales support llmclient!' The welcome messages will appear as the first assistant message in each message list from the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench, as well as any production UI that leverages the SmarterChat React.js Component - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smarter.sh/ui-prompt.
appWelcomeMessage.title: Appwelcomemessage

customDomain.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.custom_domain[str]. Optional. The custom domain to use for the llmclient. Example: example.com

defaultMaxTokens.description:
LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.default_max_tokens[int]. Optional. The default max tokens to use for the llmclient. This defaults to 2048.
The max tokens is an integer value that controls the maximum number of tokens in the llmclient's response. The maximum number of tokens is the sum of the tokens in the prompt and the tokens in the response. The maximum number of tokens varies by provider. Refer to vendor documentation as this value routinely changes as new models are released.
defaultMaxTokens.title: Defaultmaxtokens

defaultModel.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.default_model[str]. Optional. The default model to use for the llmclient. This changes routinely and is currently defaults to gpt-6-luna
defaultModel.title: Defaultmodel

defaultSystemRole.description:
LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.default_system_role[str]. Optional. The default system prompt to use for the llmclient. This defaults to the following value:
You are a helpful llmclient. When given the opportunity to utilize function calling, you should always do so. This will allow you to provide the best possible responses to the user. If you are unable to provide a response, you should prompt the user for more information. If you are still unable to provide a response, you should inform the user that you are unable to help them at this time..
The system prompt is the first message in the conversation and is used to set the context for the llmclient. It is important to keep this prompt short, as it is included in the token count for each message. The maximum length of the system prompt is 2048 characters.
defaultSystemRole.title: Defaultsystemrole

defaultTemperature.description:
LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.default_temperature[float]. Optional. The default temperature to use for the llmclient. This defaults to 1.0.
The temperature is a floating point value between 0 and 1 that controls the randomness of the llmclient's responses. A value of 0 means that the llmclient will always choose the most likely response, while a value of 1 means that the llmclient will choose a random response. Low values work better for information retrieval tasks, while high values work better for creative tasks.
defaultTemperature.title: Defaulttemperature

deployed.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.deployed[bool]. Required. Whether the llmclient is deployed. Deployed means that the llmclient is available for use outside the Smarter Prompt Engineer Workbench. Published llmclients have their own subdomain, Kubernetes ingress, and TLS/SSL certificate.
deployed.title: Deployed

provider.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.provider[str]. Optional. The provider to use for the llmclient.
provider.title: Provider

subdomain.description: LLMClient.spec.configuration.prompt.subdomain[str]. Optional. The subdomain to use for the llmclient for published public urls. Example: https://<subdomain>.3141-5926-5359.api.example.com
subdomain.title: Subdomain

SAMLLMClientSpecConfigPrompt.title: SAMLLMClientSpecConfigPrompt

SAMLLMClientSpecConfigStyles.description:
Smarter API LLMClient Manifest LLMClient.spec.config.styles.

The look of Smarter Chat for this LLMClient. Every setting is optional. See the module's docstring.

appBackgroundImageSize.description: LLMClient.styles.appBackgroundImageSize[str]. Optional. How the background image fills the conversation: 'cover' (the default) fills it and crops the image's edges, 'contain' shows the whole image, and 'auto' shows the image at its own size, repeated like tiles.
appBackgroundImageSize.title: Appbackgroundimagesize

appBackgroundImageUrl.description: LLMClient.styles.appBackgroundImageUrl[str]. Optional. The url of an image that is displayed behind the conversation. Choose a quiet image, so that the messages stay readable, or tint it with a semi-transparent messageList.backgroundColor. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/images/background.png'.
appBackgroundImageUrl.title: Appbackgroundimageurl

appLogoUrl.description: LLMClient.styles.appLogoUrl[str]. Optional. The url of the LLMClient's logo, a square image that is displayed in a circle at the left of the chat's header, and on the LLMClient's card in the web console. chatscope's Avatar. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/images/logo.png'.
appLogoUrl.title: Applogourl

assistantAvatarUrl.description: LLMClient.styles.assistantAvatarUrl[str]. Optional. The url of a small square picture, displayed in a circle beside each of the assistant's messages. chatscope's Message Avatar. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/images/assistant.png'.
assistantAvatarUrl.title: Assistantavatarurl

borderRadius.description: LLMClient.styles.borderRadius[str]. Optional. How round the corners of the message bubbles and of the message input box are. '0' is square. chatscope's $default-border-radius. Example: '0.7em' (the default) or '18px'.
borderRadius.title: Borderradius

conversationHeader.description: LLMClient.styles.conversationHeader[object]. Optional. The bar at the top of the chat.

fontFamily.description: LLMClient.styles.fontFamily[str]. Optional. The chat's fonts, the first that the visitor's browser has, in order. chatscope's $default-font-family. Example: '"Fredoka", system-ui, sans-serif'.
fontFamily.title: Fontfamily

fontSize.description: LLMClient.styles.fontSize[str]. Optional. The size of the chat's text, of which every other size is a proportion. chatscope's $main-container-font-size. Example: '16px' or '1.1rem'.
fontSize.title: Fontsize

googleFont.description: LLMClient.styles.googleFont[str]. Optional. The name of a font from https://fonts.google.com, which the chat downloads. When fontFamily is not set, the chat uses this font. Example: 'Fredoka'.
googleFont.title: Googlefont

incomingMessage.description: LLMClient.styles.incomingMessage[object]. Optional. The assistant's message bubbles, on the left.

mainContainer.description: LLMClient.styles.mainContainer[object]. Optional. The frame around the whole chat.

messageInput.description: LLMClient.styles.messageInput[object]. Optional. The box in which the user types.

messageList.description: LLMClient.styles.messageList[object]. Optional. The area that holds the conversation.

outgoingMessage.description: LLMClient.styles.outgoingMessage[object]. Optional. The user's message bubbles, on the right.

typingIndicator.description: LLMClient.styles.typingIndicator[object]. Optional. The indicator that the assistant is answering.

userAvatarUrl.description: LLMClient.styles.userAvatarUrl[str]. Optional. The url of a small square picture, displayed in a circle beside each of the user's messages. chatscope's Message Avatar. Example: 'https://cdn.example.com/images/user.png'.
userAvatarUrl.title: Useravatarurl

SAMLLMClientSpecConfigStyles.title: SAMLLMClientSpecConfigStyles
